basis: The task's rows are built from the XKDR Forum Air-Quality-Database republishing of the Central Pollution Control Board CAAQM PM2.5 stream (data.xkdr.org API, cpcb_caaqm stream; the us_embassy stations are excluded at construction). Two upstream instruments apply. (1) CPCB's own publication of the real-time AQI dataset is licensed GODL-India by the data.gov.in platform instrument: 'The content published on data.gov.in is owned by the respective Ministry/State/Department/Organization and licensed under the Government Open Data License - India' (read via Wayback snapshot 20251231005230 of the resource page 2026-11-04, because the live portal is unreachable from every project-controlled vantage; corroborated live by AIKosh, which lists 'License: GODL license' for the same dataset). GODL-India v1.0 grants a worldwide, royalty-free, non-exclusive license to use, adapt, publish and create derivative works for all lawful commercial and non-commercial purposes, with attribution (named template), non-endorsement, no-warranty and continuity conditions and NO share-alike clause. CPCB's own site copyright policy is restrictive-by-default but carries an explicit 'unless otherwise indicated' carve-out; the data.gov.in platform publication is the indicated licence for the dataset published there. (2) The XKDR Forum compilation is released under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 (Air-Quality-Database README, read 2026-11-04): 'use it for anything, including commercial work, and credit India Air Quality Database, XKDR Forum together with the sources, the Central Pollution Control Board (CAAQM network) and the US Department of State via AirNow.' Both instruments permit redistribution and derivatives with attribution. Class A. Standing defaults apply: our code and documentation are MIT, our rights in the derived compilation are dedicated CC0-1.0, and the sources' own terms are preserved, never relicensed.

compilation.scope: Our contribution - the station-day eligibility frame (complete cpcb_caaqm PM2.5 station-days, n_hours >= 18, with a labelable D+1), the derived binary next-day exceedance label (calendar-day D+1 24-hr mean PM2.5 > 90 ug/m3, the CPCB National AQI Poor-band lower breakpoint), the at-instant trailing-history feature derivations and calendar fields, the sentinel handling for stations with no state_name, the excluded-and-counted thin/unlabelable/outside-window accounting, and the temporal partition (train 2019-2022 / eval 2023 / holdout 2024) - is dedicated to the public domain under CC0-1.0. The dedication covers only our contribution: the underlying CPCB CAAQM measurements and the XKDR compilation keep their own designations and remain subject to GODL-India and CC BY 4.0 respectively, whose attribution requirements carry through to every copy of the derived data. Nothing here relicenses the source or presents CC0 as the source's terms.

source.status: Two preserved upstream instruments, neither relicensed. CPCB CAAQM PM2.5 measurements: Government Open Data License - India (GODL-India v1.0) via the data.gov.in platform instrument, with its attribution template, non-endorsement, no-warranty and continuity conditions. The XKDR Forum Air-Quality-Database compilation carrying those measurements: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0, with the README's own requested credit. The redistributed fields are the publisher's own station identifiers, timestamps and hourly PM2.5 measurements (aggregated by us to daily statistics) plus our derived label, features and partition. The derived dataset is labelled as such throughout and is neither a CPCB product nor an XKDR Forum product.

source.derived_labelling: Labelled as a derived research dataset throughout; it is neither the Central Pollution Control Board's official product nor the XKDR Forum's, and neither has reviewed or endorsed it. The publishers' own designations, requested credits and data-quality caveats are preserved ('as reported', 'no gap filling', 'preliminary and not fully validated'), and changes from the source are indicated (row selection and eligibility, the derived binary next-day exceedance label, at-instant trailing-history features, the UNKNOWN_STATE sentinel, excluded-and-counted accounting, the temporal partition).

conditions: The requested credits carry in every copy of the data and its documentation: 'India Air Quality Database, XKDR Forum' together with 'the Central Pollution Control Board (CAAQM network)' and 'the US Department of State via AirNow' (CC BY 4.0), and the GODL-India attribution template for the CPCB measurements.
GODL-India's non-endorsement condition carries through: the derived dataset is labelled as such and is not presented as a CPCB, Government of India, or XKDR Forum product.
The XKDR compilation's own data-quality caveat is preserved beside the data: values are 'as reported', with 'no gap filling', and marked 'preliminary and not fully validated'.

Changes are indicated: the dataset ships a row selection (complete cpcb_caaqm PM2.5 station-days with a labelable D+1), a derived binary next-day exceedance label at the CPCB National AQI Poor-band lower breakpoint, at-instant trailing-history features, an UNKNOWN_STATE sentinel for stations without state_name, excluded-and-counted thin/unlabelable/outside-window rows, and a temporal partition (train 2019-2022 / eval 2023 / holdout 2024).

The comparison ladder travels with every quoted figure: the runner-contract baseline (eval AUC 0.9734) is quoted beside station_persistence 0.9689 and state_season_climatology 0.8617 on the identical eval rows, with the clustered intervals; no figure may be quoted without the comparison beside it.
Our contribution is dedicated CC0-1.0; the sources' terms are preserved and carry through unchanged, including attribution.
Our code and documentation are MIT.

operator_acceptance.note: No operator acceptance is needed or recorded: both upstream instruments (GODL-India for the CPCB measurements, CC BY 4.0 for the XKDR compilation) are read open terms permitting redistribution and derivatives with attribution, and this release stays within them.
